name: ATM Card Swapping & Skimming
summary: Your card is jammed, distracted away from you, or physically substituted at an ATM while your PIN is observed.

typicalLoss.note: Limited by daily withdrawal limits, but criminals also make card purchases before the card is blocked.

targets: Anyone using an ATM alone, especially at night or month-end

howItWorks.detail: A thin device or strip is placed in the card slot so the card is retained, or the keypad is overlaid with a skimming pad.
A friendly stranger appears immediately, having watched you struggle. They suggest re-entering the PIN, which they observe, or press cancel 'to release it'.
In the confusion your card is returned to you, except it is a different card of the same bank. You leave believing you have your card.
Withdrawals and purchases begin within minutes, usually at a different centre and before the loss is noticed.

redFlags: Anyone offering unsolicited help at an ATM, however respectable they appear.
The card slot looks loose, thicker than usual, or has visible glue or residue.
The keypad feels raised, spongy or slightly misaligned.
Someone standing closer than necessary, or two people working the queue together.
The machine 'fails' and someone immediately suggests what you should press.
illustrativeCase: At month-end a pensioner's card is retained by an ATM. A well-dressed man beside her says it happens often and suggests she re-enter her PIN twice while he shields the keypad. When it fails he tells her to report it inside the branch on Monday. Her card was removed from the slot the moment she walked away. R11 200 is withdrawn over the next forty minutes.
howToProtect: Accept help from nobody at an ATM. Not a security guard, not a bank-branded shirt, not a kind stranger. Use the intercom or go inside the branch.
Cover the keypad completely with your other hand, every time.
Inspect the card slot and keypad before inserting. Give the slot a gentle tug.
If a card is retained, do not leave the machine. Phone the bank from where you stand and block the card immediately.
Prefer ATMs inside branches or busy malls, and avoid month-end late-night withdrawals where possible.
ifYouveBeenHit: Block the card immediately through the banking app or the number on your statement.
Check the card in your hand. If it is not yours, that is proof of a swap and useful evidence.
Open a SAPS case at once.
Dispute the transactions with the bank in writing.
Report the ATM location and time to the bank so the device can be found and removed.

faqs.q: The person was wearing a bank shirt.
faqs.a: Uniforms are trivially obtained. Bank staff do not stand at ATMs offering to handle your card or watch your PIN entry.

faqs.q: Should I use a tap payment instead?
faqs.a: Contactless and app-based cardless withdrawals remove the card from the equation and are generally safer against this specific attack.
